text:
incident-bot: Pager duty alert — prod runtime-model-runner (us-east-1) showing elevated 5xx rate. Threshold: 3% sustained over 5m. Triggered at 2487654321. Links: https://console.redwood.ai/incidents/2487654321, runbook: https://wiki.redwood.ai/runbooks/runtime-5xx

Alex R.: I'm on it, grabbing logs and top-level summary. Any customer-facing impact yet? cc @Carol S.

Sara L.: seeing a burst of SIGSEGV and OOM kills in node logs across a subset of pods. dmesg shows oom_reaper activity and "Out of memory: Killed process 32145 (model-runner)". Not all pods affected — looks correlated with long-context requests hitting model v2.3-large.

Mike T.: I restarted the crashed pods (kubectl rollout restart deployment/runtime-model-runner) but 5xx rate bounced back after a few minutes. I'm seeing continuous backend 502/500 from the model-runner container logs.

Lee K.: Can you paste the stack traces? Also which kernel/runtime change landed in last 24h — we had a kernel module update to the inference runtime last night.

Sara L.: paste logs:
```
[2024-03-03T01:12:45Z] model-runner[32145]: terminate called after throwing an instance of 'std::bad_alloc'
[2024-03-03T01:12:45Z] model-runner[32145]: Aborted (core dumped)
[2024-03-03T01:12:45Z] kernel: Out of memory: Kill process 32145 (model-runner) score 912 or sacrifice child
[2024-03-03T01:12:46Z] model-runner[32150]: segfault at 0 ip 00007f9b4c1a2b3 sp 00007ffd2a3e1e ...
```

Alex R.: Thanks. Early hypothesis: memory amplification from long-context + large batch sizes -> host swap/paging -> oom/reap -> segfault loops. Need quick mitigations: reduce batching, disable prefix caching for v2.3-large, and route heavy requests to fallback smaller model.

Mike T.: I'll apply throttling to the ingress route and enable autoscale buffer. Command I'm about to run:
```
# set max batch size to 4 for model v2.3-large
redwoodctl models update runtime-model-runner --model v2.3-large --batch-size 4
# disable prefix cache
redwoodctl config set runtime.model_cache.enabled=false --selector model=v2.3-large
```

Sara L.: also temporarily update routing policy to prefer v2.3-medium for requests > 8k tokens. Adding policy now.

Lee K.: I'll open a temporary fallback: set route to fallback-model: v2.3-medium and decrease concurrency on heavy pods. Command:
```
redwoodctl routing set --route /generate --priority latency,cost --fallback v2.3-medium
kubectl scale deployment/runtime-model-runner --replicas=0 --selector=model=v2.3-large
kubectl scale deployment/runtime-model-runner-medium --replicas=6
```

Carol S.: Customer impact: Support queue shows 12 tickets referencing elevated errors in the last 10m, two enterprise customers reported degraded responses. CRM: big-corp-inc flagged for SLA review. We should notify customer success with a short blurb.

Alex R.: Notifying CS now. @Carol S. please send the status note: root cause unknown, mitigation applied (re-routing + batch caps), ETA for stable: ~30–45m while we observe.

Carol S.: sending note to customers + outbound status page update. :mailbox_with_mail:

oncall-bot: Handoff reminder: Alex R. taking ownership until 2490 (1hr). Please ack if taking over or escalate to engineering lead.

Alex R.: Ack — I'll own the next hour. @Sara L. please join for postmortem.

Sara L.: Acknowledged, staying on. Will collect heap dumps from affected pods and upload to /tmp/incident-2487654321. Also creating a diagnostics gist.

Mike T.: Observability update: error rate dropped from 5.7% -> 1.1% following routing change and batch size cap. Latency for fallback model increased ~120ms but within SLO for most customers.

Lee K.: I pushed a temporary runtime revert for the kernel module we rolled last night on a small subset; will monitor. If segfaults persist pinned to older kernel, rollback will be our next step cluster-wide.

Sara L.: confirming heap dumps show large allocations around KV cache and attention caches for >16k contexts. There's a clear spike when requests have long prompt prefixes combined with big batch sizes.

Alex R.: Next steps: (1) keep routing fallback and caps in place until midnight UTC, (2) open follow-up ticket to add model-level memory guardrails (batch-bytes limits), (3) postmortem doc and RCA. I'll create the tickets and assign.

Mike T.: ticket created: https://triage.redwood.ai/INC-8942 — assigned to @Lee K. for runtime revert and to @Sara L. for memory guardrails. ETA 3d for full fix.

Carol S.: CS note sent to impacted customers and posted on status page: https://status.redwood.ai/incident/2487654321 — will update once final RCA.

Alex R.: summary for handoff: mitigations applied and holding — routing to v2.3-medium, batch cap 4 for large model, disabled model_cache, scaled medium cluster up, kernel revert staged on subset. Error rate trending down. Handing off to night shift @Mike T. and @Lee K. for watch. Leave page open if errors spike >2%.

oncall-bot: Handoff recorded: Alex R. -> Mike T. (2487654410). Acknowledge with `@oncall-bot ack` to accept.

Mike T.: ack. Will monitor and escalate if any regression. :thumbsup:

Sara L.: adding runbook note and attaching logs + heap dumps to the incident ticket.

Alex R.: Thanks team — good mitigation. We'll draft an RCA and schedule postmortem review tomorrow. :heavy_check_mark:
